audit(cpp): coroutine and callback lifetime audit of the native gateway, area A: runtime network layer

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-x1-20261118-44302040764-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: `cpp/gateway/` is a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway. Read `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (coroutine rules), `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (build driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config asan --shard N/4`) and `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-clang-tidy-audit-20261117.md` first. Three other agents audit the other source areas at the same time; stay in yours.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these)
- `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-lifetime-a-20261118.md` (your report) and `cpp/gateway/analysis/lifetime/a/` (scripts and `sites.json`). Do NOT change production code or tests: the maintainer dispatches fixes from your list.

HARD WORKING RULE (a previous attempt at this audit lost five hours of analysis because it kept findings in memory and the model connection restarted ten times): your process WILL be restarted without warning, and after a restart you know only what is committed. Therefore: create the report in the first five minutes with a checklist of every file in your area; after EVERY file you finish, append its sites and verdicts to the report and to `sites.json`, tick the file, and `git commit`; never go more than 15 minutes without a commit. On start (and after any restart) read your report first and continue from the first unticked file. Do not spend more than 20 minutes on tool setup: if clang-tidy over a file is slow or fails, read the file and classify by reasoning.

TASK
This code base is a mechanical port of asynchronous TypeScript onto C++20 coroutines (Boost.Asio awaitables behind JavaScript-style `Promise`/`Task` wrappers in `include/uos/rt/async.hpp`). In JavaScript closures keep their captured state alive; in C++ they do not, and one confirmed memory-safety defect of this class was already found and fixed (`src/admin/kernel.cpp`: coroutine lambdas capturing handler locals, awaited through a fail-fast `rt::all` that does not cancel siblings, so a still-pending sibling resumed into a destroyed frame; see `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-clang-tidy-audit-20261117.md` and the rule added to `PORTING.md`). An earlier audit judged 25 further sites safe, but it was done quickly and before large refactors. Audit every first-party file in YOUR AREA: `cpp/gateway/src/rt/{async,abort,clock,process_loop,stream,fetch*,tls*,http,websocket*,gzip}.*` and the matching headers under `cpp/gateway/include/uos/rt/`. Look for these lifetime hazards across suspension points: (a) coroutine lambdas with captures (by reference or by value: the closure object itself must outlive the coroutine) whose returned task can outlive the enclosing scope (passed to `rt::all`/`allSettled`/`race`, stored, detached with `spawn`, returned); (b) coroutine functions taking reference or `string_view`/`span` parameters that are used after the first `co_await` while the caller may not keep the referent alive; (c) `this` captured in callbacks registered on longer-lived objects (sockets, timers, abort signals, streams) without ownership, and the reverse (ownership cycles that leak: several were found by sanitizers in `runtime/http*.cpp`, `codex/supervisor_transport.cpp`, `provider/stream_relay.cpp`); (d) iterators or references into containers held across `co_await` while another coroutine can mutate the container; (e) structured bindings or temporaries bound directly to a `co_await` expression (a known GCC 12 miscompile pattern the port forbids). Use clang-tidy (`cppcoreguidelines-avoid-capturing-lambda-coroutines`, `cppcoreguidelines-avoid-reference-coroutine-parameters`, `misc-coroutine-hostile-raii`, `bugprone-dangling-handle`, `bugprone-use-after-move`; the tree has `cpp/gateway/.clang-tidy` and `tools/tidy.sh`) and grep-based finders for `co_await`, lambda coroutines, `spawn`, `rt::all`/`allSettled`/`race` and callback registration; then READ every site and classify it: DEFECT (the failing interleaving in two lines and a minimal proposed diff), SAFE (one line: who owns what), or UNCLEAR (what you would need to decide). Rank defects: memory safety on a request path first. Where cheap, confirm a DEFECT with a focused AddressSanitizer test kept outside the checkout (describe it and give the command in the report).

DONE WHEN
Every file in your area is ticked, every site has a verdict in the report and in `analysis/lifetime/a/sites.json`, and the report ends with a ranked DEFECT list with proposed diffs and counts per class. If time runs short, what is committed must already be a correct partial list.
